record.title: China's MIIT sets network-admission and distribution controls for agent-enabled terminals
record.summary: China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published notice 工信厅信管〔2026〕42号 on 6 November; the notice is dated 24 October. It covers agents preinstalled on phones, tablets and wearables. The original Chinese text calls for compatibility checks and compatible-device lists, risk assessment in network-admission testing, advance plans and ministry review for live over-the-air upgrades, and app-distribution checks that include developer declarations on agent invocation. The notice also refers to the agent-interconnection national-standards series: the SAMR catalogue lists GB/Z 185.2-2026 (identity code) and GB/Z 185.3-2026 (identity management) as current guidance, while Parts 8 (audit) and 9 (transaction) are still listed as drafting projects. This establishes published documents and their catalogue status, not detailed implementation, enforcement or outcomes.
organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published notice 工信厅信管〔2026〕42号 on 6 November 2026; the document itself is dated 24 October 2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice addresses preinstalled agents on phones, tablets and wearables. It calls for compatibility verification and user-facing compatible-device and operating-system lists; agent compatibility and fraud-risk assessment in telecom network-access testing; advance submission and review of plans for live over-the-air upgrades; and app-distribution checks, including developer declarations on whether agents may invoke applications.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The text and publication do not establish an implementation date, completed standards, enforcement activity, the number of affected devices, compliance, or measured safety, market or economic outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The SAMR national-standards catalogue lists GB/Z 185.2-2026 (Agent Interconnection, Part 2: Identity Code) and GB/Z 185.3-2026 (Part 3: Identity Management) as current guidance documents, each published 22 May 2026. The catalogue lists Parts 8 (Agent Audit) and 9 (Agent Transaction) as projects in drafting.

evidence_gaps.description: Although the notice points to the agent-interconnection standards series and the catalogue lists current identity-code and identity-management guidance, this check did not inspect the full standard text or determine how the agent identity code is bound to the terminal/device identity, tested or implemented.
No compliance, enforcement, market-coverage or user-safety outcome is available in the notice itself.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, the notice could shape compatibility testing, network admission, in-service upgrades and app distribution for agent-enabled phones, tablets and wearables in China. Its implementation and market effects are not yet measured.
limitations: The notice was issued on 24 October and published on 6 November; the online publication date is the recent public-disclosure event recorded here.

The notice and national-standards catalogue were directly inspected, but the full normative text of GB/Z 185.2-2026/185.3-2026, their mapping to terminal identifiers, implementation standards, enforcement records, compliance measures, device inventories and outcome studies were not inspected or found in this bounded check.
No inference is made that the notice has already changed device behavior, app distribution or user safety.
organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China
brief.summary: China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published notice 工信厅信管〔2026〕42号 on 6 November; the notice is dated 24 October. It covers agents preinstalled on phones, tablets and wearables. The original Chinese text calls for compatibility checks and compatible-device lists, risk assessment in network-admission testing, advance plans and ministry review for live over-the-air upgrades, and app-distribution checks that include developer declarations on agent invocation. The notice also refers to the agent-interconnection national-standards series: the SAMR catalogue lists GB/Z 185.2-2026 (identity code) and GB/Z 185.3-2026 (identity management) as current guidance, while Parts 8 (audit) and 9 (transaction) are still listed as drafting projects. technical.claimed_result: The official notice states requirements and procedures for agent-enabled terminal compatibility, network admission, in-service upgrades and app distribution. No real-world effect is measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The original Chinese MIIT notice and its issue/publication metadata were directly inspected.
technical.mechanism: The notice sets out compatibility verification and user-visible device/OS lists; agent-related network-admission and fraud-risk testing; advance reporting and post-upgrade ministry review for live OTA changes; and app-distribution checks, developer declarations and compatibility listing. The referenced series already includes current guidance documents for agent identity code and identity management; separate audit and transaction parts remain in the drafting stage in the SAMR catalogue.
technical.regime: Chinese telecom terminals with agents preinstalled, including phones, tablets and wearables. The notice is dated 2026-10-24 and was published online 2026-11-06. Detailed standards and implementation coverage remain unknown. SAMR lists GB/Z 185.2-2026 and GB/Z 185.3-2026 as current, both published 2026-05-22; the full documents were not inspected.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to this policy-document claim; implementation and outcome claims remain unverified.
technical.strongest_baseline: The MIIT notice and SAMR standards catalogue are primary sources for the published policy text and the listed status of the referenced standards. Neither source establishes field implementation or effect.

brief.title: China's MIIT sets network-admission and distribution controls for agent-enabled terminals
brief.why_it_matters: The notice links terminal compatibility, network-admission testing, upgrade procedures and app-distribution consent to China’s existing agent-interconnection standards. GB/Z 185.2-2026 and GB/Z 185.3-2026 are listed as current guidance for identity code and identity management; the catalogue still lists audit and transaction parts as drafts. Practical device coverage, enforcement and effects remain unestablished.
